events.description:
From Silicon Valley to Helsinki: What Finnish Founders Learned in the AI Capital
Finnish founders who've been in the thick of the San Francisco AI scene share what they saw, what they learned, and what it means for building here.
The Bay Area is where the AI hype machine runs loudest – but what's real and what's noise? Finnish founders who've spent time in the Silicon Valley ecosystem are coming back with perspectives that's hard to get from a LinkedIn feed.
AI Collective Finland is bringing together founders from Switch and Homie – companies that have been on the ground in San Francisco – for an evening of honest conversation about what the SF AI scene actually looks like up close, and what Finnish builders can take from it.
Who this is for
Founders, operators, executives, team leads in B2B or SaaS companies who want to understand what the current AI landscape looks like and how it can impact your business – whether you're at 10 people or 500.
People looking for their next role at fast-moving AI companies. Both Switch and Homie are actively hiring – this is a chance to meet the founders and teams directly.
Anyone in the Finnish tech scene curious about what's actually happening in San Francisco and if it's something you want to try.
How the evening works
We hear from founders sharing their experience – what they saw in the Silicon Valley AI ecosystem, how it compares to building in the Nordics, and what they're bringing back.
After that, a 30-minute panel digs into the real questions: what's overhyped, what's underrated, and what does it actually take to compete from Helsinki?
The floor opens for audience Q&A, and the night ends with networking.

Building an AI prototype has never been easier.
A few prompts, a model API, some data — and you can have something impressive running in days.
But then reality hits.
Real users. Real data. Real security requirements. Real integrations. Real costs. Real failures.
The gap between an impressive AI demo and a production-ready product is where many teams get stuck.

Where AI products typically break when real users arrive

Data, security, integrations, latency and cost

AI feature:
User → prompt → model → response
AI-powered product:

Just a practical conversation about the engineering, product and operational decisions that turn an AI experiment into something people can actually rely on.

events.name: Journey to the Centre of the LLM
events.description: Tokyo Tech Talks #8, "Journey to the Centre of the LLM," is coming up on Tuesday, September 29. We usually encounter a large language model from the outside. We give it words, it gives us words back, and almost everything in between stays hidden. On September 29, independent researcher [Larry Richards](https://lbrichards.github.io/research-notes/) will guide Tokyo Tech Talks beneath that familiar surface. Through experiments with model internals, we will explore what happens inside an LLM and what those internal behaviors can tell us about how it works. Larry studies mechanistic interpretability, sparse representations, activation interventions, and the geometry of language-model internals. He also created and maintains [vollib](https://vollib.org/), an open-source library available in Python and TypeScript for option pricing, implied volatility, and Greeks. This session assumes a basic understanding of Transformer models, including layers, activations, and next-token prediction. It focuses on experimental exploration rather than introducing Transformer architecture from the beginning. If you would like to prepare, [3Blue1Brown's visual introduction to Transformers](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/gpt/) is an excellent foundation.
events.descriptionSummary: Independent researcher Larry Richards—who specializes in mechanistic interpretability and maintains the open-source vollib library—will crack open the black box of large language models by diving into their internal mechanics through hands-on experiments, revealing what actually happens beneath the surface when these models process language.

events.name: BRISA Reading Group 05 - Embodied Intelligence via Learning and Evolution
events.description:
We're continuing our reading group series: for our fifth session we will look at the paper Embodied Intelligence via Learning and Evolution (Gupta, Savarese, Ganguli & Fei-Fei, 2021) from Stanford, published in Nature Communications and with open code on GitHub.
In our very first session, Play2Perfect had a robot learn to play before it learned to assemble and the discussion turned to evolution and how it relates to reinforcement learning. This time, we follow that thread directly.
Most robot learning treats the body as fixed and asks how to learn a controller for it. This paper makes the body part of the search.
An outer evolutionary loop mutates simulated creatures by adding, deleting and reshaping their limbs and joints. An inner RL loop then trains a controller for each new body from scratch. How well that controller performs at the end of training decides whether the body gets passed on.
Nothing learned is inherited. Every child starts with a randomly initialised controller, and nothing in the setup rewards learning quickly. Even so, within ten generations, the training time needed to reach a fixed level of performance drops by half.
There's also a very practical side. The full run used 1,152 CPUs and finished in under 16 hours. One small design choice, removing the oldest agent instead of the weakest, lets the system survive failing machines, so it can run on cheap spare cloud capacity.
And a broader one: should we keep designing robot bodies by hand and learn only the controller, or should the body be learned too?
No preparation needed. Skim the abstract if you have ten minutes. Everyone is welcome - whatever you study, wherever you study and however much robotics you have done so far.
Come with questions, disagreements, or your own take on how much of intelligence lives in the body.

🎟️ There are only a limited number of spots, so we can keep the session personal and interactive. Please register early and only attend if you've received a ticket.
📍 Hosted at the Merantix AI Campus on September 22nd. Doors open 18:30, we start at 18:45.

Agents are changing what is possible, and their greatest potential emerges when they collaborate safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.
Participants will form teams on the day, develop a working prototype and present it at the end of the event. Each team will explore how open-source collaborative agents of varying complexity can work together safely.

Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system using Flower in which the safe collaboration of agent teams is central to the solution.

Automate a task
Form self-improving loops with one another
Operate across distributed machines and datasets

events.description: Shaping our future with AI. Creating opportunity through AI fluency, connection and community. No jargon. No hype. No confusing terminology. **Join us for our next in-person meetup in London on Tuesday 29th September.** The theme of this meetup is **"Did AI Break Recruitment?"** AI can rewrite your CV, apply for jobs, screen CVs and even interview candidates but are these tools really helping? As hiring managers and recruiters struggle to filter through the noise, job seekers (especially those with unconventional career paths) can find themselves filtered out without a human ever reviewing their unique experience. Candidates can generate tailored CVs in minutes; employers can screen at scale. The result can feel like an arms race of volume, keywords and automated filtering. This session explores a more human alternative: **AI that helps people understand, own and communicate their real experience with confidence.** Using Career Core as a live case study, the talk shows how a single, evidence-based career record can support accurate CVs, targeted applications, strengths reflection and better career decisions — without AI inventing someone’s story. events.description: Hello and welcome to our joint meetup between AWS AI UK, Azure AI UK, and GCP AI UK. This crossover event brings together AI engineers, cloud architects, data practitioners, platform engineers, and technology leaders exploring how agentic AI is reshaping the way software gets built and delivered across all three major clouds. This is a special Community Stack ecosystem event, bringing together several of our cloud- and AI-focused communities for an evening of practical talks, hands-on technical discussion, and cross-community networking. A huge thank you to Digital Futures for hosting and sponsoring this event, and for supporting the growth of the cloud and AI community in London. **Speakers and sessions:** **Building Agents in Azure: A Crash Course** Lisa Carpenter, Practice Director, Digital Futures Building production-ready generative AI agents no longer requires a specialist team. In this session, Lisa will show how Azure's Python framework supplies the tools, orchestration, and guardrails needed to move from prototype to production quickly, and where to begin on your own agentic journey. As Practice Director at Digital Futures, Lisa leads all training and learning initiatives, ensuring the Frontier AI Programme is designed to meet client needs while empowering consultants with the skills and confidence to thrive in their digital careers. Her work sits at the heart of Digital Futures' mission of turning potential into capability and curiosity into lifelong growth. Before stepping into her leadership role, Lisa built a career helping organisations unlock value from their data, designing technical solutions and statistical models that turned information into meaningful insight. Her journey took a transformative turn in 2018, when she discovered her passion for developing people. Since then, she has been dedicated to creating and delivering data and technology education that inspires and transforms. Lisa is a champion of digital empowerment and ethical innovation. She firmly believes that anyone can learn to harness technology to make their work more creative, efficient, and impactful, and that responsibility and ethics must always guide how data and AI are used for the benefit of humanity. Outside the world of data and learning, Lisa is an avid boulderer and can often be found paddleboarding along Regent's Canal. **Harness Engineering: Building Your Lean, Mean Delivery Machine** Jaroslav Pantsjoha, Technical Director, Nearform What multiplies output is not the model, it is the harness around it: the codified context, skills, hooks, sub-agents, and humans, all aligned on new ways of working, with an SME squad or operators to leverage the potential. One rule makes the whole thing work: lean context engineering. And the part Jaroslav genuinely did not see coming was that codifying the AI forced the humans to align, quicker and sooner. In this session, Jaroslav will unpack a real harness he runs on Google Cloud, delivering with a fraction of the planned team at a throughput that sounds made up until you see the headcount delta. He will also cover the foobars and the parts that still need tuning every single week. The weekend pioneer who ships miracles is real and worth talking about. But how many pioneers does your organisation have, and can you run an enterprise on pioneers alone? This talk is about how you get from one to many, and how to work through the transformation of the developer. events.name: Flutter Paris is back with an AI special
events.description: C'est le grand retour du Flutter Paris 🥳 ! Après quelques mois en sommeil, nous profitons de cette rentrée pour lancer une nouvelle saison. Pour l'occasion, nous serons accueilli chez [Ippon Technologies](https://fr.ippon.tech/) pour découvrir deux présentations **1️⃣ 1ère présentation 🇬🇧 (Sasha Denisov)** **Edge AI in Flutter: How Far Have We Come?** When flutter_gemma shipped its first release two years ago, on-device AI in Flutter was real but narrow: a MobileNet-class classifier for vision, and a small, text-only LLM wrapped over MediaPipe that answered one prompt at a time — no images, no tools, no memory. In 2026 the picture is almost unrecognizable: your phone runs a multimodal open model — Gemma, Qwen, Llama, and more — that sees images, calls tools, remembers context, and retrieves from a local knowledge base, entirely offline, with nothing ever leaving the device. This talk is a retrospective on how we got here — across the models, the runtimes that execute them (Google's LiteRT-LM and MediaPipe, other engines like llama.cpp and ONNX Runtime, and even the model the OS now ships itself), and the Dart packages that made all of it native to Flutter. As a throughline, we'll follow flutter_gemma: how it grew, release by release, from a thin MediaPipe wrapper around a 2B model into a modular ecosystem of its own — pluggable engines, embeddings, on-device RAG, and agents that call tools, run skills, and even speak MCP — and where it goes next. Along the way we'll trace what changed in the silicon (CPU → GPU → NPU) and the developer experience, and look honestly at what's production-ready today. **2️⃣ 2ème présentation 🇬🇧 (Elaine Dias Batista)** **Flutter development in the AI era** Description communiquée ultérieurement **🎁 Surprise, surprise** Nous aurons également une très bonne nouvelle à vous partager…

events.name: Embodied AI NYC
events.description:
Join us for Embodied AI NYC, an evening exploring what happens when intelligence enters the physical world.
From our first conversation with ChatGPT to talking naturally with AI or watching an agent use a computer, we’ve had moments when a new possibility suddenly clicked. What are those moments for physical AI systems?
Through live demos, creative experiments, and conversations with artists, researchers, designers, and builders, we’ll explore machines that learn from us, respond to our input, express themselves, and find their way through unexpected situations.
We’re interested in both what these systems can do and how we experience them: the gestures that make control intuitive, the movements that communicate intent, and the design choices that help a machine feel at home in our lives.
Come discover something unexpected, meet the people making it possible, and leave with an idea to bring into your own work.
Hosted at ZeroSpace, a next-gen production and creative studio specializing in the integration of digital, virtual, and live content.
🎙️ Demos & Conversations
Charlotte Kemp Muhl & Sage Morei, FINIS MUSICAE
Finis Musicae, a futurist art and transhuman tech collective, is applying robotics as the next step in the evolution of music performance.
Sebastian Marino, Monumental Labs
Monumental Labs is building an AI-powered robotic fabrication platform that bridges the workshop traditions of fine arts with cutting-edge technology to make magnificent sculpture and stone architecture accessible at scale.
Remaining lineup TBA.
🛠️ Share Your Work
Building something in physical AI, robotics, or human–machine interaction? We’d love to hear from you. Research prototypes, creative experiments, and works in progress are welcome. Fill out our speaker interest form to tell us what you’d like to share.

events.name: UGLY TALK: THE BUSINESS OF BEING A CREATOR AND Q4 WELCOME PARTY
events.description:
The algorithm can make you a celebrity overnight. It can also shadowban you without telling you. Your email list and your community stay with you. The question is how to make the most of them.
This Ugly Talk is about the business side of being a creator, whether you're a YouTuber, streamer, podcaster or blogger. What has AI changed about how you work, research and produce? What does your audience want from you now? Which calls do creators wish they'd made sooner, and which tools are they actually using?
After the talk, we're throwing Q4 a welcome party for you. Food and drinks are on the house. Come to enjoy yourself and meet other creators and the brands that want to work with them.
🎯 Why you should be in this room.
Get a clear view of the creator business in 2026, including what has changed since 2023, what no longer works, and what is likely coming in 2027.
Learn which AI tools creators are actually using, how to treat AI as a teammate instead of a threat, and what changing audience expectations mean for creators and brands.
Meet NYC creators, brand operators, and community builders at the Q4 welcome party. Food and drinks are on the house, and eligible attendees receive a 30-day Kit trial plus a free recording session at Kit Studio.

Schedule a time that fits your schedule

💬 What's on the table.
The creator business in 2026: what is working, what is not, and which assumptions from 2023 need to be retired.
What is likely to shape creator businesses in 2027, including revenue models, brand partnerships, owned audiences, and community.
The latest AI tools creators are using for research, production, distribution, and operations, plus how to use AI as a teammate instead of a threat.
How audience expectations are changing and what creators need to pay attention to before their audience tells them the hard way.
What brands need from creators now, and how founders and operators can enter the creator space without forcing a strategy that does not fit.
🎤 Featured speakers.

Haley Janicek - Head of Creator Community, Kit
Haley Janicek is Head of Creator Community at Kit, and she's spent nearly a decade being in the room with creators in person, well before it was popular. She leads Craft + Commerce, Kit's longstanding creator conference, doing everything from booking speakers and sponsors to selling tickets and picking the venue. Most recently, she led the Kit Studios initiative, growing it to three physical locations in Boise, Chicago, and New York. Before Kit, she spent 15 years in SaaS. She lives in Boise, Idaho, and travels far too often.

Matt Mitsui - Founder, CCExNYC
Matt Mitsui is the founder of Content Creators Exchange of New York, a monthly gathering where New York's content creators meet the people they'd otherwise only follow - across every level, from first upload to full-time. Over roughly three years he has run 48 events and built a community of more than 2,000 members on Meetup, with every flagship event free to attend. He spends most of his time on the unglamorous side of creator work: logistics, partnerships, and building rooms where people actually meet their next collaborator.

Gabby Beckford - CEO, Packs Light
Gabby Beckford builds her creator business, @packslight, like an engineer: testing, measuring, and rebuilding rather than chasing trends. It's allowed her to not only survive but scale for 6 years through three completely different eras of the internet: the blog era, the short-form video boom, and now the AI shift changing how audiences find and trust creators. She's grown to 800K+ followers across platforms, partnered with brands from Disney to Microsoft Copilot, and now splits her time between nurturing her Travel and Lifestyle community and advising brands on exactly these creator economy shifts as they evolve.

Ayanna Dutton-Diaz - Founder, AD Consulting
Ayanna Dutton-Diaz is a brand strategist, speaker, and Founder of AD Consulting. She works with founders and multi-hyphenate leaders ready to stop limiting themselves to one identity and build a brand that finally reflects who they actually are. Drawing on 15+ years inside global brands including LinkedIn, Meta, and Cadillac, she equips leaders with the clarity and language they need to find their through line and build presence that opens doors. Past stages include Goldman Sachs One Million Black Women x Brooklyn Public Library LevelUP, LinkedIn x Cannes Lions, The One Club for Creativity, Luminary, and The Female Quotient. She co-founded Non-Corporate Girls™ and writes The Aya Brand on Substack. Whether through keynotes, workshops, or panel moderation, she leaves every room with something they can use.

Join us for Agentic + AI Observability meetup on Tuesday, September 29 from 5pm - 8pm PST at the Databricks Bellevue office, an evening focused on agentic architectures and AI observability: architecture, governance, and real-world deployment of AI agents.
This meetup is built for engineers, ML/AI practitioners, and AI startup founders who are already experimenting with agents (or planning to) and want to go deeper into the tech. We’ll cover real-world patterns, failure modes, and tooling for building a reliable meta-harness layer to manage agent execution, control and choice, state, and runtime policies across the broader ecosystem.
Whether you’re at an early-stage startup or an established company, if you care about getting AI agents into production and keeping multi-agent systems healthy, this meetup is for you.

See real architectures: Learn how teams are designing the meta-harness layer on top of data/feature platforms, isolated sandboxes, and tools, separating model reasoning from system execution.
Learn how to observe what agents are doing: Go beyond logs and dashboards to structured traces, evals, and metrics that help you audit meta-harness behavior, enforce cost budgets, and track agent choices.
Connect with other builders: Meet engineers, founders, and practitioners working on similar problems, swap meta-harness design patterns, and find collaborators and potential hires.
